summary: De-esser with a band-pass detector on the sibilance band: Relative (the band's level against the whole signal's, for vocals: it follows the singer's level) or Absolute (the band's level against the threshold). The reduction is made on a split band (minimum phase, or linear phase with latency) or on the whole signal as a dynamic high shelf or bell. Lookahead, Listen (hear what the detector hears), Delta (hear only what is taken out) and a gain-match reading. Use it for sibilance on vocals, harsh cymbals and hats, or a bright master.
use_for: Tame harsh s and t sounds in vocals and bright sources.

parameters.name: Detector
parameters.description: Relative: the band's level against the whole signal's (follows the singer). Absolute: the band's level in dBFS
parameters.how: Chooses what the detector compares: Relative uses the band against the whole signal, Absolute uses the band's level in dBFS.
parameters.sound: Relative follows the singer's level so quiet and loud passages are treated alike; Absolute reacts only when the band gets loud.

parameters.name: Frequency
parameters.how: Sets the centre of the sibilance band, from 2 to 16 kHz.
parameters.sound: Aim it at the harsh hiss of the voice, typically 5 to 9 kHz, so only that sound is turned down.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Width of the band in octaves: the detector's band, the split band and the bell
parameters.how: Sets how wide the band is, from 0.5 to 3 octaves.
parameters.sound: A narrow band targets one harsh note; a wide band calms a broad, hissy zone but touches more of the voice.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Where reduction starts: Relative, the band's level under the whole signal's; Absolute, dBFS
parameters.how: Sets the level, from -60 to 0 dB, above which the band is reduced.
parameters.sound: Lower values catch more sibilants; set too low, the voice sounds dull and lispy.

parameters.name: Ratio
parameters.description: How much of the excess is taken out: 1 nothing, 20 nearly all
parameters.how: Sets how much of the excess above the threshold is removed, from 1:1 (nothing) to 20:1 (almost all).
parameters.sound: Higher ratios make the s sounds smaller and more uniform.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Split: only the band is reduced, minimum phase, no latency of its own. Split linear: the band by a linear-phase filter (latency 255 samples). Shelf: a dynamic high shelf on the whole signal. Bell: a dynamic bell
parameters.how: Chooses how the band is reduced: Split (only the band), Split linear (linear phase, with latency), Shelf (dynamic high shelf) or Bell.
parameters.sound: Split sounds the most transparent, Shelf darkens the whole top end, and Bell is a gentle dip around the band.

parameters.name: Max reduction
parameters.description: The most the de-esser takes out
parameters.how: Limits how much the de-esser can take out, from 0 to 24 dB.
parameters.sound: A small range keeps it natural; a large one removes sibilance fully but can sound lisping.

parameters.name: Attack
parameters.description: How fast the reduction comes in
parameters.how: Sets how fast the reduction comes in, from 0.1 ms to 20 ms.
parameters.sound: Fast attacks catch short s sounds; slow ones let the start of each hiss through.

parameters.name: Release
parameters.how: Sets how fast the reduction lets go, from 10 ms to 0.5 s.
parameters.sound: Short releases follow each syllable closely; long ones can dull the sound after a sibilant.

parameters.name: Lookahead
parameters.description: Delays the audio so the reduction is in place when the sibilant arrives (latency)
parameters.how: Delays the audio by up to 5 ms so the reduction is in place when the sibilant arrives.
parameters.sound: The first part of each hiss is caught cleanly, at the cost of a little latency.

parameters.name: Listen
parameters.description: Hear the band the detector hears
parameters.how: Switches the output to the band the detector hears.
parameters.sound: You hear only the sibilance range, which helps you place Frequency and Width exactly.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the de-esser, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)
parameters.how: Adds -24 to +24 dB of gain after the de-esser.
parameters.sound: It matches the loudness to the untreated voice so you can judge the tone fairly.

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what the de-esser takes out: the output minus the input, delayed to match (glides over 10 ms)
parameters.how: Plays only the difference between the output and the input.
parameters.sound: You hear exactly what the de-esser removes, so you can check it is taking hiss and not the voice's body.

readings.description: The reduction now, dB (0 or more)
The lookahead (plus the linear-phase split's 255), reported to NeoBuzz Live
